markscheme.html:
Correct answer: B

A: Slower motion gives a smaller rate of change of magnetic flux, so the induced emf (and deflection magnitude) is not the greatest.

B: Faster motion gives the largest rate of change of magnetic flux, so the induced emf magnitude (and hence galvanometer deflection magnitude) is greatest.

C: Reversing direction/polarity reverses the deflection direction, but the slow speed means a smaller flux change rate than the fastest case, so not the greatest magnitude.

D: If the magnet is stationary, the magnetic flux through the coil is constant, so and there is no induced emf or deflection.

question.html:
A coil is connected to an ideal galvanometer. A bar magnet is pushed into the coil. Which combination results in the greatest deflection of the galvanometer?

Magnet motionMagnet polarity facing coil
A. Slowly inwardNorth pole
B. Quickly inwardNorth pole
C. Slowly outwardSouth pole
D. StationaryEither pole
  1. Slowly inward | North pole
  2. Quickly inward | North pole
  3. Slowly outward | South pole
  4. Stationary | Either pole
